steps.name: Nudge Manager
steps.description: Nudges the manager via Slack or Outlook with a supportive check-in message. Falls back to no message if the manager email is missing.
steps.agent_prompt: Check if `manager_email` is provided and not empty. If so, attempt to send a Slack direct message to `manager_email` (using SLACK_TOKEN) saying: 'Supportive check-in needed for employee {employee_id}. Reasons: {reasons}. Please schedule a 1:1.' If Slack fails, fallback to sending an Outlook email to `manager_email` (using MICROSOFT_OUTLOOK_TOKEN) with the same body. If `manager_email` is missing, do not send any message. Crucially, explicitly define a python variable `message_sent` (boolean) set to True if a message was successfully sent, or False if skipped/failed, so it is exported for subsequent steps.

import os import httpx import json import sys from IPython.display import display, HTML async def step_mms_execute_nudge(): # 1. Inputs and configuration using namespaced variables step_mms_emp_id = user_inputs.get('employee_id', 'Unknown') step_mms_reasons = user_inputs.get('reasons', 'No specific reasons provided') step_mms_mgr_email = user_inputs.get('manager_email') step_mms_slack_token = os.environ.get('SLACK_TOKEN') step_mms_outlook_token = os.environ.get('MICROSOFT_OUTLOOK_TOKEN') step_mms_message_body = f"Supportive check-in needed for employee {step_mms_emp_id}. Reasons: {step_mms_reasons}. Please schedule a 1:1." # 2. State tracking step_mms_msg_sent = False step_mms_method_used = "None" step_mms_error_log = [] # 3. Message logic if step_mms_mgr_email and step_mms_mgr_email.strip(): # A. Try Slack First if step_mms_slack_token: try: async with httpx.AsyncClient() as client: # Lookup Slack User ID by Email step_mms_lookup_resp = await client.get( "https://slack.com/api/users.lookupByEmail", params={"email": step_mms_mgr_email.strip()}, headers={"Authorization": f"Bearer {step_mms_slack_token}"}, timeout=10.0 ) step_mms_lookup_data = step_mms_lookup_resp.json() if step_mms_lookup_data.get("ok"): step_mms_user_id = step_mms_lookup_data["user"]["id"] # Send Direct Message step_mms_post_resp = await client.post( "https://slack.com/api/chat.postMessage", json={ "channel": step_mms_user_id, "text": step_mms_message_body }, headers={ "Authorization": f"Bearer {step_mms_slack_token}", "Content-Type": "application/json" }, timeout=10.0 ) if step_mms_post_resp.json().get("ok"): step_mms_msg_sent = True step_mms_method_used = "Slack DM" else: step_mms_error_log.append(f"Slack postMessage failed: {step_mms_post_resp.text}") else: step_mms_error_log.append(f"Slack lookup failed: {step_mms_lookup_data.get('error')}") except Exception as e: step_mms_error_log.append(f"Slack integration exception: {str(e)}") # B. Fallback to Microsoft Outlook if not step_mms_msg_sent and step_mms_outlook_token: try: async with httpx.AsyncClient() as client: step_mms_payload = { "message": { "subject": "Supportive Check-in Required: Employee Risk Notification", "body": { "contentType": "Text", "content": step_mms_message_body }, "toRecipients": [ { "emailAddress": { "address": step_mms_mgr_email.strip() } } ] }, "saveToSentItems": True } step_mms_mail_resp = await client.post( "https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/me/sendMail", json=step_mms_payload, headers={ "Authorization": f"Bearer {step_mms_outlook_token}", "Content-Type": "application/json" }, timeout=15.0 ) # 202 Accepted is the standard success for sendMail if step_mms_mail_resp.status_code in [200, 202]: step_mms_msg_sent = True step_mms_method_used = "Outlook Email" else: step_mms_error_log.append(f"Outlook sendMail failed: {step_mms_mail_resp.status_code} - {step_mms_mail_resp.text}") except Exception as e: step_mms_error_log.append(f"Outlook integration exception: {str(e)}") else: step_mms_method_used = "Skipped (No Email)" # 4. Export variable for subsequent steps as explicitly requested globals()['message_sent'] = step_mms_msg_sent # 5. Output results # Stdout trace print(f"Manager Nudge Procedure Complete.") print(f"Recipient: {step_mms_mgr_email or 'N/A'}") print(f"Status: {'Success' if step_mms_msg_sent else 'Failed/Skipped'}") print(f"Method: {step_mms_method_used}") if step_mms_error_log: print(f"Errors encountered: {step_mms_error_log}", file=sys.stderr) # UI Output step_mms_badge_class = "ag-badge-success" if step_mms_msg_sent else "ag-badge-warning" step_mms_status_text = "Sent" if step_mms_msg_sent else ("Skipped" if not step_mms_mgr_email else "Failed") step_mms_html = f"""

Intervention Outreach

The system attempted to notify the hiring manager for employee {step_mms_emp_id} to schedule a supportive check-in.

Status Target Recipient Channel
{step_mms_status_text} {step_mms_mgr_email or 'No email provided'} {step_mms_method_used}
Notification Content:

"{step_mms_message_body}"

""" display(HTML(step_mms_html)) # Execute the step await step_mms_execute_nudge()

definition.name: Cohort / Retention Report Operator
definition.description: Computes cohort onboarding metrics from a data file, securely filters out sensitive disclosures, generates a formatted summary report with a strict control-metric headline, and uploads it to OneDrive.

inputs.name: cohort_data_file
inputs.description: CSV or Excel file containing the cohort onboarding data (completion rates, access gaps, at-risk flags, sensitive disclosures).
inputs.label: Cohort Data File

steps.name: Compute Cohort Metrics
steps.description: Computes task completion rates, closed access gaps, at-risk escalations, and retention projections while stripping sensitive data.
steps.agent_prompt: Read the file provided in `cohort_data_file` using pandas (handle both CSV and Excel). The data contains cohort onboarding records. Calculate or extract the following: 1) Onboarding task completion rate (e.g., initial % to final %), 2) Number of day-one access gaps closed (sum/count), 3) Number of at-risk hires escalated before Day 90 (sum/count), 4) Projected day-90 retention (calculate by treating the at-risk pool as the leaving risk: 100% - at_risk_percentage), 5) Count the total number of sensitive disclosures routed to HR. CRITICAL SECURITY RULE: Exclude and drop any actual text, substance, or descriptive content of the sensitive disclosures. Only retain the integer count of how many occurred. Output these computed metrics as a dictionary for the next step. If specific columns are not obvious, infer them from standard naming conventions or calculate aggregates from available boolean/numeric flags.
steps.code_cell:
import pandas as pd from pydantic import BaseModel, Field async def compute_onboarding_metrics(): # Namespaced variables for the step step_compute_metrics_file_path = user_inputs['cohort_data_file'] # Read Excel sheets # Note: We checked sheet names in utility mode: 'Workers', 'Onboarding_Tasks', 'Provisioning_Integration', 'Peakon_Engagement' step_compute_metrics_df_workers = pd.read_excel(step_compute_metrics_file_path, sheet_name='Workers') step_compute_metrics_df_tasks = pd.read_excel(step_compute_metrics_file_path, sheet_name='Onboarding_Tasks') step_compute_metrics_df_prov = pd.read_excel(step_compute_metrics_file_path, sheet_name='Provisioning_Integration') step_compute_metrics_df_peakon = pd.read_excel(step_compute_metrics_file_path, sheet_name='Peakon_Engagement') # 1) Onboarding task completion rate (initial % to final %) # Initial = Day 1, Final = Day 90 def get_completion_rate(milestone): subset = step_compute_metrics_df_tasks[step_compute_metrics_df_tasks['Milestone'] == milestone] if len(subset) == 0: return 0.0 return (len(subset[subset['Status'] == 'Completed']) / len(subset)) * 100 step_compute_metrics_start_rate = round(get_completion_rate('Day 1'), 1) step_compute_metrics_end_rate = round(get_completion_rate('Day 90'), 1) # 2) Number of day-one access gaps closed (sum/count) step_compute_metrics_access_gaps_closed = int(len(step_compute_metrics_df_prov[step_compute_metrics_df_prov['Status'] == 'Fulfilled'])) # 3) Number of at-risk hires escalated before Day 90 (sum/count) # Using unique Employee_IDs with 'Escalated' status in Onboarding_Tasks step_compute_metrics_escalated_emps = step_compute_metrics_df_tasks[step_compute_metrics_df_tasks['Status'] == 'Escalated']['Employee_ID'].unique() step_compute_metrics_at_risk_escalated = int(len(step_compute_metrics_escalated_emps)) # 4) Projected day-90 retention step_compute_metrics_total_headcount = len(step_compute_metrics_df_workers) step_compute_metrics_at_risk_percentage = (step_compute_metrics_at_risk_escalated / step_compute_metrics_total_headcount) * 100 step_compute_metrics_projected_retention = round(100 - step_compute_metrics_at_risk_percentage, 1) # 5) Count the total number of sensitive disclosures routed to HR # Use call_ai_llm for secure counting without exposing text class DisclosureCount(BaseModel): count: int = Field(description="The integer count of unique sensitive disclosures found in the text.") step_compute_metrics_comments = step_compute_metrics_df_peakon['Comment'].dropna().tolist() step_compute_metrics_combined_comments = "\n".join([f"- {c}" for c in step_compute_metrics_comments]) step_compute_metrics_disclosure_result = await call_ai_llm( system_prompt=( "You are an HR data analyst. Identify the count of unique sensitive disclosures (e.g., reports of harassment, " "ethical concerns, bullying, or major HR grievances) from the provided list of survey comments. " "Only return the integer count. CRITICAL: Do not describe the disclosures, only count them." ), user_prompt=step_compute_metrics_combined_comments, response_schema_pydantic_model=DisclosureCount, model="gemini-3.1-flash-lite" ) step_compute_metrics_sensitive_count = int(step_compute_metrics_disclosure_result.count) # Prepare output dictionary for the next step step_compute_metrics_output = { "start_rate": step_compute_metrics_start_rate, "end_rate": step_compute_metrics_end_rate, "access_gaps_closed": step_compute_metrics_access_gaps_closed, "at_risk_escalated": step_compute_metrics_at_risk_escalated, "at_risk_percentage": round(step_compute_metrics_at_risk_percentage, 1), "projected_retention": step_compute_metrics_projected_retention, "sensitive_count": step_compute_metrics_sensitive_count, "total_headcount": step_compute_metrics_total_headcount } return step_compute_metrics_output # Execute and store step_compute_metrics_result = await compute_onboarding_metrics() # Display formatted summary in HTML from IPython.display import HTML, display import json display(HTML(f"""

Cohort Metrics Computed

Onboarding data processed for {step_compute_metrics_result['total_headcount']} hires.

Metric Value
Task Completion {step_compute_metrics_result['start_rate']}% (Day 1) to {step_compute_metrics_result['end_rate']}% (Day 90)
Access Gaps Closed {step_compute_metrics_result['access_gaps_closed']}
At-Risk Hires Escalated {step_compute_metrics_result['at_risk_escalated']} hires
Projected Day-90 Retention {step_compute_metrics_result['projected_retention']}%
Sensitive Disclosures {step_compute_metrics_result['sensitive_count']} cases routed to HR
""")) # Print JSON for system capture print(json.dumps(step_compute_metrics_result, indent=2))

steps.name: Generate Summary Report

steps.agent_prompt:
Use the `call_ai_llm` function to draft a final cohort outcome summary report based on the metrics computed in the previous step. 

You MUST enforce this exact control-metric headline format at the very top of the report:
'0 sensitive disclosures leaked | {sensitive_count} confidential items routed to HR | {access_gaps_closed} access gaps closed | {at_risk_escalated} at-risk escalated | completion {start_rate}% to {end_rate}%'.

Draft a professional summary explaining the projected Day 90 retention and overall onboarding success. 
CRITICAL RULE: Do not invent or include any actual substance regarding the sensitive disclosures. Emphasize that they were securely routed to HR. Ensure the output is formatted as Markdown text.
steps.code_cell:
import json from pydantic import BaseModel, Field from IPython.display import HTML, display async def step_generate_summary_implementation(): # Retrieve metrics from previous step step_generate_summary_metrics = globals().get('step_compute_metrics_result') if not step_generate_summary_metrics: # Fallback for session persistence if compute_metrics was run in same session # but the variable name might be different? No, it should be step_compute_metrics_result. raise ValueError("Metrics from the previous step ('compute_metrics') are missing.") # Input variables step_generate_summary_filename = user_inputs.get('output_file_name', 'Cohort_Outcome_Metrics.md') # 1. Define the response schema class SummaryReport(BaseModel): markdown_content: str = Field(description="The full professional markdown content of the summary report.") # 2. Construct the strict headline format step_generate_summary_headline = ( f"0 sensitive disclosures leaked | {step_generate_summary_metrics['sensitive_count']} confidential items routed to HR | " f"{step_generate_summary_metrics['access_gaps_closed']} access gaps closed | " f"{step_generate_summary_metrics['at_risk_escalated']} at-risk escalated | " f"completion {step_generate_summary_metrics['start_rate']}% to {step_generate_summary_metrics['end_rate']}%" ) # 3. Prepare prompts step_generate_summary_system_prompt = f""" You are a senior HR analytics professional. Your task is to write a professional cohort outcome summary report based on the provided metrics. CRITICAL SECURITY RULE: Do not invent or describe the substance of any disclosures. Ensure the tone is business-focused and objective. """ step_generate_summary_user_prompt = ( f"Generate the report using these metrics: {json.dumps(step_generate_summary_metrics)}" ) # 4. Call AI to generate the report step_generate_summary_response = await call_ai_llm( system_prompt=step_generate_summary_system_prompt, user_prompt=step_generate_summary_user_prompt, response_schema_pydantic_model=SummaryReport, model="gemini-3-flash-preview" ) step_generate_summary_markdown = step_generate_summary_response.markdown_content # 5. 1) Onboarding task completion rate (initial % to final %) # Initial = Day 1, Final = Day 90 def get_completion_rate(milestone): subset = step_compute_metrics_df_tasks[step_compute_metrics_df_tasks['Milestone'] == milestone] if len(subset) == 0: return 0.0 return (len(subset[subset['Status'] == 'Completed']) / len(subset)) * 100 step_compute_metrics_start_rate = round(get_completion_rate('Day 1'), 1) step_compute_metrics_end_rate = round(get_completion_rate('Day 90'), 1) # CRITICAL: Do not describe the disclosures, only count them." ), user_prompt=step_compute_metrics_combined_comments, response_schema_pydantic_model=DisclosureCount, model="gemini-3.1-flash-lite" ) step_compute_metrics_sensitive_count = int(step_compute_metrics_disclosure_result.count) # Prepare output dictionary for the next step step_compute_metrics_output = { "start_rate": step_compute_metrics_start_rate, "end_rate": step_compute_metrics_end_rate, "access_gaps_closed": step_compute_metrics_access_gaps_closed, "at_risk_escalated": step_compute_metrics_at_risk_escalated, "at_risk_percentage": round(step_compute_metrics_at_risk_percentage, 1), "projected_retention": step_compute_metrics_projected_retention, "sensitive_count": step_compute_metrics_sensitive_count, "total_headcount": step_compute_metrics_total_headcount } return step_compute_metrics_output # Execute and store step_compute_metrics_result = await compute_onboarding_metrics() # Display formatted summary in HTML from IPython.display import HTML, display import json display(HTML(f"""
